questions.question: Distinguish between urban and rural areas and give one example of how they depend on each other.
questions.expected_answer: Urban: towns and cities with dense populations working mostly in secondary and tertiary industries. Rural: countryside with farms and villages, sparse population, mainly agriculture, mining, forestry and tourism. Link e.g.: rural areas supply food and raw materials to cities; cities supply goods, services and jobs; city workers send remittances to rural relatives.

questions.question: Name three challenges faced by rural areas and three faced by urban areas.
questions.expected_answer: Rural (any three): few jobs; dependence on grants and remittances; poor roads, water, electricity and internet; clinics and schools far away; lack of farming inputs and markets; out-migration of young people. Urban (any three): informal settlements and housing backlog; unemployment; overloaded water, power and refuse services; crime; traffic and long commutes; pollution, fires and floods.

questions.question: Explain urbanisation using one push factor and one pull factor, and suggest one solution for a rural area.
questions.expected_answer: Urbanisation is the growth in the share of people living in urban areas. Push e.g. lack of jobs or services in rural areas; pull e.g. job opportunities, schools, hospitals in cities. Solution e.g.: build roads and infrastructure, support small farmers, develop tourism, expand internet access.
